notes: Backend: the default Provider of dsh-mnemon is Mnemon Native, a thin driver over the separate `mnemon` CLI (npm @mnemon-dev/mnemon 0.2.13, Go binary, SQLite). dsh-mnemon itself holds no retrieval index for Memory Spaces; the CLI returns scored candidates and dsh-mnemon applies its quality policy and per-turn admission.

Write path: the default product write path is an LLM-driven idle review / distillation that decides what to store. No LLM budget: memories were written verbatim through the explicit remember API (service.remember, defaults category=general, importance=3, source=user, no tags/entities). The review step was bypassed and is not measured. llm_tokens=0.

Dates: `mnemon remember` has no date argument (created_at = now). Memories were written in date order within seconds; the memory dates are not represented in the store, so any recency/temporal signal of the CLI sees all memories as written at the same moment.
Dedup/conflict detection of the CLI stayed on. Actions returned by remember: {"added":240}. Rows stored: 240 of 240.

ranked uses a second service instance configured with the built-in policy exhaustive-v1 (no score threshold, no tier caps), limit 10, inspect=true (readonly snapshot). Items that carry score 0 are still listed in CLI order. The CLI itself fetches a pool of 40 for smart recall; with embeddings the driver re-ranks that pool by vector similarity.

deployed = the model-facing first Recall call of one turn under the default Layered strategy. dsh-mnemon does NOT inject Memory Space recall automatically before a turn; the model has to call the recall tool (the resident runtime-memory source, which is separate hot memory and is not benchmarked, is the only thing always injected). A quiet question therefore only returns nothing if the model calls recall and the policy admits nothing; a model might also skip the call.
deployed scores are 0 for every item: the strategy admission (boundedModelInsights) drops the score field before the model sees the result; order is the admitted order.

deployed ms covers the whole strategy read (service.search incl. the `mnemon` process launches, any lexical-recovery call, admission), measured around that call only. Each launch is a new process (node launcher -> native binary).

Ordering side effect: deployed runs a live (non-readonly) recall, which records access counts for returned candidates and may influence later questions, as in real use; ranked runs first, readonly, on the same state. Questions were run in id order.

deployed = the memory injection message the pre-step hook adds before the user message; the adapter runs the plugin's registered pre-step handlers as a chain with a stand-in agent whose message has source kind user. The injected items carry no ids: an item is matched to a memory by its full text, and an item the plugin shortened (over 500 characters, or over the rest of the 2000-character budget; it ends with the plugin's fixed suffix) by its unique prefix. A shortened memory counts as delivered and is marked `shortened`; `chars` is the length of the item as injected. Items that match no memory count as noise.

The plugin recalls from the second user message of a session; every question session first receives one fixed unrelated message. Each question uses a fresh session object (recall state is per session).

Recall rows carry the topic key (the memory id) and the descriptor; ids are read from the key. memory_search results are read the same way. The recall block returns rows without scores: deployed scores are rank-derived.
ms times the soul:recall provider only (it lists and reads every topic file through the plugin's mtime cache and scores them).

notes: INGESTED 240 of 240 memories as episodes (name = memory id); failed episodes: 0; not ingested: 0. If this is below 240 it is a SUBSET: the 127 memories that are expect/stale for some question were taken first, the remaining ones in date order while the 5 CNY budget lasted. The scorer still scores all 160 questions, so questions whose memories were not ingested cannot be answered.
Failed episode ids: none

ranked and deployed are the SAME call: Graphiti.search(query) = recipe EDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF (BM25 + cosine over facts, RRF), default limit 10. Returned items are fact edges. Mapping: an edge maps to the memory of the earliest episode in edge.episodes (by memory date); several edges from one memory keep the best position; unmappable -> null. search() returns no scores, so score = 1/rank (order only).

Tool has no date argument: Date.now() was set to each memory's date (12:00 UTC + index seconds) during ingest, and to the day after the last memory (2026-10-21) for all questions. ranked = memory_search tool with k=10 and a fresh session per question (blind top-5 plus 5 unseen). The tool returns hits re-sorted by updated_at; the adapter restores retrieval order from explain.bm25 * explain.recencyWeight.

Usage stats (hit_count, last_accessed_at) are reset by direct SQL after each call so all questions see the same state; this only undoes the side effect of the lookup and does not influence ranking logic.

notes: Memories were written directly as memory files (content/write, mode create) under events/YYYY/MM/DD/<id>.md with the memory date in the path; OpenViking's session/commit extraction (which needs a language model) was not used, so llm_tokens is 0. A real deployment would extract facts with a model, which this does not measure.

Embeddings: bge-m3 (1024) through the shared embedder; indexing is asynchronous, ingest_seconds includes the wait until a sample of 21 memories (and the last one written) found themselves (wait 69.2 s; writes alone 2.6 s, 0 write failure(s)).
Scores are OpenViking's own search scores, not comparable across systems.
deployed: the plugin's default limit/threshold is UNVERIFIED (its package is not available offline); the API defaults stand in for it: limit 10, no score threshold. So deployed equals ranked in size.
The search over viking://~/memories also returns directory summaries (.abstract.md/.overview.md): 8 such item(s) among the ranked results of all questions.
0 question(s) failed (empty lists).
ms is one find call with the API defaults, measured inside the container, including the server's query embedding through the shared embedder.
An OV background task may try to summarise directories with its language model; no key and no internet are available, so those attempts fail harmlessly and do not affect file search.
This file drops results that are not memory files (id would be null).

caveat.zh: 直接写记忆文件，不走会话提取（真实部署会用模型提取，这里没测）；API 默认值，没有阈值，交付约 10 条；默认插件设置未能核实。
caveat.en: Memory files written directly, no session extraction (a real deployment extracts with a model; not measured); API defaults, no threshold, about 10 items delivered; the plugin's own defaults could not be verified.

seekmemory-aged-detail.mode: verbatim ingest as level=detail memory artifacts via the kernel's persist(), no extraction, no embeddings (SeekMemory has no vector search), no LLM; deployed = recall.pipeline.query_block with default config (recall_k 8, budget 600 chars, evidence gate, disclosure); AGED: after ingest, clock advanced 365 days with zero recalls, maintain.decay.decay_all swept (240 memories forgotten), then the questions were answered
seekmemory-aged-detail.how: store.open_store(':memory:'); store.sources.append_sources([Source]); maintain.link.persist(make('memory', ...), artifacts, cache, graph); maintain.decay.decay_all(artifacts, cache, today); deployed: recall.pipeline.query_block(cache, graph, artifacts, sources, umo, text, private=True, conf=DEFAULTS, owner_umo, speaker, hybrid_retriever=HybridRetriever) -> info['final_ids']; ranked: HybridRetriever.retrieve + recall.score.select(k=10, gate=False, explore=0)
notes: decay_all(today=2027-11-14) marked 240 of 240 memories state=forgotten (reversible revision, row kept); no recall happened between ingest and the sweep.
Clock for the aged run: container date 2026-11-14 + 365 days = 2027-11-14; decay_all takes it as a parameter, recall.score/temporal/assemble `date` rebound for the run.

Write path: Source row (memory text, owner, one private session) + maintain.link.persist (commit + cache.put + link_new graph edges). Extraction is skipped because it needs an LLM; the artifact text is the memory text verbatim. No tags, no emotion values (defaults), shape=point, about=other, scope=private, said_by/subject_id=owner. The dataset fields source and kind were not given to the system.
level=detail was chosen before the first run: 'fact' is the level for plain statements; maintain.decay.decay_plan never forgets level=fact (maintain/expiry_policy.py:49-50).

Not applied because they need an extraction model: tags, arousal/valence, 'supersedes' (the only mechanism that retires an older memory when a newer one contradicts it). Updated questions therefore rely on ranking alone.

ids: the artifact id is the memory id; deployed ids come from info['final_ids'] (items that reached the assembled block, after the 600-char budget). Scores are rank-derived (1/rank) because select() and query_block return no scores; they carry no meaning across systems.

ranked: pool and scope-prior weighting replicate query_block; select(k=10, gate=False, explore=0). It bypasses the intent switch (intent 'none' for greetings/clock/operate words) and disclosure so it measures retrieval only. deployed keeps both.
deployed uses defaults including explore_rate 0.1 (seeded by the query text, may swap the last pick for a random lower-ranked one) and the recent-context fallback for profile/topic questions.
A persistent HybridRetriever is used (as in the host adapters); BM25 index builds on the warm-up query.
0 question(s) with an error; 160 deployed call(s) returned an empty block.

caveat.zh: 365 天老化实验，不是默认运行：记忆按 detail 级写入，老化后 240 条全部被标记为遗忘，什么都召回不到（Hit@5 0%，安静率 100%）。
caveat.en: A 365-day ageing experiment, not a default run: memories written at detail level, all 240 are marked forgotten after ageing, so nothing is recalled (Hit@5 0%, quiet rate 100%).
